b2-06-01.title: Communicative Challenge: In Front of the Colours
b2-06-01.scenario: At dusk the young painter has walked into the walled garden, and the old master asks how he looks at the flowers. You (the painter) say that you are standing in front of the colours, entranced.
b2-06-01.prompt: Tell the master how you are standing in front of the colours in his garden.
cues: Say how you feel as you look
Say what you are standing in front of
b2-06-01.english: I am standing in front of the colours, entranced.
b2-06-01.canDo: I can form adverbial participles with -va/-ve across regular and irregular verb stems (állva, mosolyogva, elragadtatva)

b2-06-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Gate of the Garden
b2-06-02.scenario: At the gate of the walled garden the young painter explains to the old master how he got in. You (the painter) say that the gate was not locked, only pulled shut.
b2-06-02.prompt: Tell the master what state the gate was in.
cues: Say that the gate was not locked
Say what state it was in instead
b2-06-02.target: A kapu nem volt zárva, csak be volt hajtva.
b2-06-02.english: The gate was not locked, it was only pulled shut.
b2-06-02.canDo: I can use van/volt/lesz + -va/-ve to describe the visible resulting state of a completed action (meg van világítva, ki van állítva)

b2-06-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Why I Came In
b2-06-03.scenario: In the walled garden the old master asks the young painter why he came in although the garden is closed at this hour. You (the painter) answer that you knew it was closed, yet came in.
b2-06-03.prompt: Tell the master why you came in, in an elevated style.
cues: Say what you knew about the garden
Say that you came in anyway
b2-06-03.target: Tudván, hogy a kert ilyenkor zárva van, mégis bejöttem.
b2-06-03.english: Knowing that the garden is closed at this hour, I came in anyway.
b2-06-03.canDo: I can recognize and form the high-register causal-anterior participle in -ván/-vén (tudván, látván, lévén)

b2-06-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Rejecting the Old Rules
b2-06-04.scenario: The old master asks the young painter what he wanted to paint in his new picture of the garden. You (the painter) say that, rejecting the old rules, you painted the inner light.
b2-06-04.prompt: Tell the master what you rejected and what you painted instead.
b2-06-04.target: A régi szabályokat elvetve a belső fényt festettem meg.
b2-06-04.english: Rejecting the old rules, I painted the inner light.
b2-06-04.canDo: I can build complex analytical sentences that chain adverbial participles (-va/-ve) with object and instrumental complements

b2-06-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Night in the Studio
b2-06-05.scenario: The next day the old master asks the young painter what he did after leaving the garden. You (the painter) say that you returned to your studio, filled with a new vision, and worked all night.
b2-06-05.prompt: Tell the master what you did after the garden.
cues: Say how you felt when you left the garden
Say where you went and what you did all night
b2-06-05.target: Új látomással eltelve visszatértem a műterembe, és egész éjjel dolgoztam.
b2-06-05.english: Filled with a new vision, I returned to the studio and worked all night.
b2-06-05.canDo: I can seamlessly integrate manner participles (-va/-ve), stative resultatives (van + -va/-ve), and causal participles (-ván/-vén)

b2-06-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Garden Taught
b2-06-consolidation.scenario: Before the young painter leaves the garden, the old master asks what he has learned. You (the painter) say that, growing quiet, you looked at the garden and saw the inner light.
b2-06-consolidation.prompt: Tell the master what you learned from looking at his garden.
cues: Say how you looked at the garden
b2-06-consolidation.target: Lecsendesedve néztem a kertet, és láttam a belső fényt.
b2-06-consolidation.english: Growing quiet, I looked at the garden and saw the inner light.
b2-06-consolidation.canDo: I can form and deploy adverbial participles of manner (-va/-ve), stative resultatives (van + -va/-ve), and literary causal participles (-ván/-vén)
